title: Operational Alerts Agent
what: An n8n workflow that acts as a watchdog: every hour it checks the status of a service or an API in your business (your website, your ordering system, a count of pending cases), compares what it sees against thresholds you define, and if anything falls outside the norm, it sends you a Telegram alert with the exact reason. If everything is fine, it stays quiet. It turns "is everything still working?" into a channel that only speaks up when there's something to look at.
forWho: For whoever is responsible for keeping something running (a website, an order queue, an inbox with an SLA) and today finds out about problems when a customer calls. It pays for itself from the first scare it saves you: setting it up takes about an hour.
capabilities: Checks your service's status URL every hour (or at whatever pace you configure)
Evaluates thresholds you write in a code node: status other than ok, more than N pending cases, whatever you define
Sends a Telegram alert only when there's an incident, with the specific reason and the time of the check
Stays silent when everything is fine: zero noise, every alert means something
Logs every check in n8n's execution history, so you can reconstruct when a problem started
limits: Fixes nothing: it just warns. Intervening on the monitored system is a human job
Doesn't replace professional monitoring with on-call rotations and escalation: it's the first step, good enough for small businesses
Doesn't detect what the checked URL doesn't report: if your status API lies, the watchdog lies with it
If n8n itself is down, there's no watchdog: for critical services, add a second, external watchdog

parameters.content:
## Vigilante horario con alerta por Telegram
Schedule → consultar tu servicio → evaluar umbrales → si hay incidencia, Telegram; si no, silencio.

Antes de activar: 1) cambia la URL del nodo «Check service» por la de tu API o página de estado, 2) ajusta los umbrales en «Evaluate thresholds», 3) credencial del bot de Telegram y tu chat_id.

Este flujo solo avisa: nunca toca el sistema vigilado.

nodes.name: Check service
nodes.notes: Transport errors continue as an error item and must be evaluated downstream.

files.name: sample-thresholds.md

setup.title: Import the workflow
setup.action: In n8n: Workflows → Add workflow → ⋯ → Import from file, and paste the JSON from the flow field.
setup.expect: 6 nodes and a note: trigger, check, evaluation, IF, and the two outputs.

setup.title: Point the watchdog at your service
setup.action: Open "Check service" and change the URL to your API or status page. If you don't have one, start by monitoring your own public website.
setup.expect: Running the node alone (Execute step), you see your service's real response.
setup.stuck: If your API requires a key, configure Authentication → Generic Credential Type → Header Auth and store the key in a credential, not in the URL.

setup.title: Define your thresholds
setup.action: Open "Evaluate thresholds" and adapt the ifs to the actual fields your service returns (check the output of the previous step). Delete any sample rules that don't apply.
setup.expect: Running the node you see alert: true or false with a coherent reason.
setup.stuck: This page's sample-thresholds.md file has ready-to-copy patterns.

setup.title: Connect Telegram
setup.action: Create the bot with @BotFather (/newbot), save the token as a Telegram credential in n8n, send a first message to your bot, and put your chat_id in the "Telegram alert" node.
setup.expect: Running the Telegram node manually, you get a test message.
setup.stuck: Without that first message from you to the bot, Telegram won't let it write to you: it's their antispam rule.

setup.title: Force a test alert
setup.action: Temporarily lower a threshold to a value you know will be exceeded (e.g. pending > 0) and run the whole workflow with Test workflow.
setup.expect: Alert on Telegram with the reason and time. Set the threshold back to its real value afterward.
setup.stuck: If it doesn't arrive, open the execution: if the IF sent the item down the false branch, your test condition wasn't really met.

setup.title: Activate and tune the pace
setup.action: Set the workflow to Active. If your service is delicate, lower the interval in "Every hour" (reasonable minimum: 5-10 minutes); if it's low-risk, raise it to 2-4 hours.
setup.expect: The execution history shows periodic checks and Telegram only rings for incidents.

test.name: Normal test
test.input: Run Test workflow with the service working and real thresholds.
test.expect: A green execution ending in "No incidents". No Telegram message.

test.name: Simulated incident
test.input: Temporarily change the URL to one that doesn't exist (e.g. add /down) and run it.
test.expect: The workflow detects the failure (empty response or error) and the alert arrives with the reason. Restore the URL.

test.name: Threshold exceeded
test.input: Lower the pending threshold to 0 and run with real data.
test.expect: Alert with the real value and threshold: "There are N pending cases (threshold: 0)".

test.name: Silence when it should be silent
test.input: Leave it active for a full day with no incidents.
test.expect: Hourly executions in the history and zero messages: the channel only speaks when there's something to say.

credentials.name: Telegram bot
credentials.how: Copy the token into an n8n Telegram credential; get your chat_id (e.g. with @userinfobot) and paste it into the alert node.

credentials.name: Your monitored API's key (only if required)
credentials.where: The dashboard of the service you're monitoring
credentials.how: Store it as an n8n Header Auth credential on the "Check service" node; never in the URL or in code.
credentials.cost: depends on the service; monitoring your own website is free

risks: False alarms that train the team to ignore the channel. Mitigation: realistic thresholds, and a fixed rule: every alert is either acted on or the threshold gets adjusted; ignoring it isn't an option.
False sense of security: the watchdog only sees what the URL reports. Mitigation: check once a month that the status API reflects reality (take down a test service and confirm it triggers).
Watchdog down without anyone knowing (n8n stopped). Mitigation: check the execution history every Monday; for anything critical, add a second, free external uptime check.
Exposing an API key in the URL. Mitigation: keys always go in n8n credentials; if one ended up in a shared URL, revoke it.

examples.name: Monitor your website
examples.prompt: Change the URL to https://yourcompany.com, enable the status code inclusion in Options, and use the "live website" threshold from the sample file.

examples.name: Second recipient
examples.prompt: Duplicate the "Telegram alert" node, set your on-call colleague's chat_id, and connect it to the true branch of the IF as well.
